history.summary: The Dhanbad centre of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON), the Gaudiya Vaishnava movement brought to the West in 1965 by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada. ADDRESS AMBIGUITY: official site iskcondhanbad.com says 'Temple | Jagjivan Nagar, Dhanbad'; listings show Bungalow 23, Old Doctor's Colony, Jagjiwan Nagar (826007), 21 Dhruv Singh Colony, Rahargora Rd, Dhaiya (826004), and Kusum Vihar — treat the Jagjiwan Nagar address as primary. The founding date of the Dhanbad centre itself was not found online. The temple follows the standard ISKCON daily schedule with Mangala Aarti, Darshan Aarti, Bhagavatam class and Sandhya Aarti; phone +91 99030 13399.

name: ISKCON Dhanbad
town_description: Dhanbad is the second-largest city in Jharkhand and is widely known as the Coal Capital of India, home to extensive coal mines and the headquarters of Bharat Coking Coal Limited. It is a major railway junction on the Grand Chord line and hosts the Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines), established in 1926. The city mixes an industrial character with green belts and serves as a gateway to nearby attractions like the Maithon and Panchet dams, Topchanchi Lake and the Parasnath Hills.
